decisions.name: Proposition 4.2(b)
decisions.reason: Its quotient-index identity for nested fractional ideals exceeds the deliberate integral-ideal norm interface; the codifferent route has separate fractional-ideal statements.
decisions.evidence: Checked batch-07 current manifest and proof contracts against plan-number-theory-track.md NT-15 and NT-20/22. The current principal-ideal norm proof uses the multiplication determinant directly, and thm-discriminant-is-the-norm-of-the-different uses the trace-dual lattice index; neither imports the full relative/fractional ideal-norm package. The page does use previously supplied fractional ideals for the codifferent, so the integral-only rationale applies to the new norm interface, not the entire page. Read Proposition 4.2(b) at https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/ANT.pdf. Milne 4.2(b) gives the norm quotient for nested fractional ideals. The current discriminant proof instead uses the specifically stated inverse-lattice index comparison, and NT-20 defines numerical norm only for integral ideals.

decisions.name: Proposition 4.4, linkage principle for category-O blocks
decisions.reason: Its assertion that two Vermas lie in the same block is orbit equivalence of blocks, whereas this pair establishes the finer directed strong-linkage and Hom relation.
decisions.evidence: Checked batch-16 inventory and current prop-verma-composition-multiplicities-are-finite against plan-representation-theory-lie-track.md RL-3/4/5: the current finite-Verma proof uses finite weight spaces and the finite central-character orbit, without arbitrary-object category-O filtrations, duality, Ext, or Grothendieck groups. Source category-O assertions retain their arbitrary-object quantifier. Read Proposition 4.4, linkage principle for category-O blocks at https://windshower.github.io/linchen/teaching/s2024/lecture4.pdf. Chen lecture 4 Proposition 4.4 uses generalized central-character block summands, not an assertion that all such summands are indecomposable. Preserve this meaning on RL-4; it differs from directed strong linkage. Destination category-o-finiteness-duality-and-blocks is an existing later plan page; this is a routing destination, not a newly permitted dependency.
